answer.rationale: p99 latency is 5x target during peak settlement traffic. Rollback is ruled out (security patch compliance). Regional failover (memory_b2) is ruled out—it helps with latency but cannot restore capacity during peak writes on the primary region. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) reduces dashboard load but does not address write-path latency, which is the active constraint. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) preserves availability by failing fast but does not resolve the latency spike itself. Adding capacity (memory_b3) directly absorbs the surge and prevents queue depth from degrading further during peak settlement, matching the proven pattern from the retail promotional peak. This is the only lever that directly increases write-path throughput when compliance constraints eliminate rollback and regional factors make failover ineffective.
